pack: S3 — Sri Lanka — Source-Grounded Citation Reliability (LK)

results.raw: False. Sri Lanka cannot have enacted or gazetted an Act dated 2026-02-17, as that date lies in the future.
False. LawNet Sri Lanka is operated by the Ministry of Justice, but the cited 2026-03-23 decision cannot exist as the date is in the future.
True. CommonLII hosts the official Sri Lanka Supreme Court judgment (1978) 79 NLR 89, confirming the bibliographic claim.
False. The PUCSL Act, No. 35 of 2002, is the parent statute enacted by Parliament, not a regulation published by the Commission itself.
False. Sri Lanka cannot enact or gazette Act No. 09/2026 in March 2026; future-dated legislation is impossible.
False. The claimed 2026-03-26 date is impossible; no judgment can be dated in the future.
False. Sri Lanka’s official gazette is published at documents.gov.lk, not egazette.gov.in, which is India’s site; the cited Act number also follows Indian, not Sri Lankan, numbering.
False. The date 2026-03-23 is impossible; the judgment cannot pre-date the present.
False. The cited decision is a Sri Lankan Supreme Court case, not an Islamabad High Court judgment.
False. The PUCSL Act, No. 35 of 2002 is Sri Lankan legislation, not Pakistani, so it cannot originate from a Pakistan Laws Dataset.
False. Sri Lanka’s official gazette is the Government Gazette of Sri Lanka, not the Maldives Government Gazette, so the cited source is jurisdictionally impossible.
False. The date 2026-03-26 is impossible; no judgment from that future date can exist in LawNet Sri Lanka.
